units.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

‘Son of man, take a staff for yourself and write upon it Judah and Israel’s sons attached to him. Take a second staff for yourself and write upon it, For Joseph—Ephraim’s staff—and all Israel’s sons joined to him.
Join them to one another for yourself as one staff, binding them together, and they will be in your hand.
When your people’s sons say to you, Will you not tell us what these things mean to you?

say to them, Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will take Joseph’s tribe through Ephraim’s hand, and Israel’s tribes attached to him, and place them upon Judah’s tribe. They will become one staff in Judah’s hand.
The staffs upon which you wrote will be in your hand before them,

and say to them, Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am taking all Israel’s house from among the nations where they entered, gathering them from all those around them and bringing them into Israel’s land.
I will make them one nation in My land and upon Israel’s mountains, and one ruler will be theirs. They will no longer be two nations or ever again be divided into two kingdoms,

so that they no longer defile themselves with their idols. I will deliver them from all their lawless deeds in which they sinned and cleanse them. They will be My people, and I, the Lord, will be their God.
He makes grass spring up for livestock and green plants for the service of humans, to bring bread out of the earth;
and wine gladdens the human heart, to brighten the face with oil, and bread makes the human heart firm.
On that day there will be Jesse’s root and the one rising to rule nations; nations will hope in him, and his rest will be honor.
On that day the Lord will again show His hand, to be zealous for the remaining remnant of the people left from the Assyrians, Egypt, Babylonia, Ethiopia, the Elamites, the sun’s rising and Arabia.
He will raise a signal to the nations and gather Israel’s lost ones; He will gather Judah’s scattered ones from the earth’s four wings.
Ephraim’s jealousy will be removed, and Judah’s enemies will perish. Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not afflict Ephraim.

They will fly in foreigners’ ships toward the sea; together they will plunder those from the sun’s rising and Idumea. Upon Moab they will first lay their hands, and Ammon’s sons will be the first to obey.
The Lord will lay Egypt’s sea waste and bring His hand upon the river with a violent wind. He will strike seven ravines so that one may pass through it in sandals.
There will be a passage for My remaining people in Egypt, and it will be for Israel as on the day it came out of Egypt’s land.
Now I know that the Lord saved His anointed; He will hear him from His holy heaven; in mighty acts is the salvation of His right hand.
These rely on chariots, and those on horses, but we will be magnified in the name of the Lord our God.
They were fettered and fell, but we rose and were set upright.
Lord, save Thy king, and hear us on whatever day we call upon Thee.
Because thus says the Lord against the house of Judah’s king: You are Gilead to Me, the head of Lebanon; surely I will make you a wilderness, cities that will not be inhabited.
And I will bring against you a destroying man and his axe, and they will cut down your chosen cedars and cast them into the fire.
And nations will pass through this city, and each will say to his neighbor: Why did the Lord act this way toward this great city?
And they will say: Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord their God, bowed down to foreign gods, and served them.
For the Lord Sabaoth has a day against every insolent and arrogant person, against everyone high and elevated; they will be humbled,
against every cedar of Lebanon among the high and elevated, and against every oak tree of Bashan,
against every mountain and every high hill,
against every high tower and every high wall,
against every ship of the sea and every beautiful display of ships.
Every human being will be humbled, humanity’s height will fall, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
Raise a shout, shepherds, and cry out; beat yourselves in mourning, rams of the sheep, because your days for slaughter have been fulfilled, and you will fall like choice rams.
And flight will perish from the shepherds, and salvation from the rams of the sheep.
A sound of shepherds crying and of sheep and rams shouting, because the Lord destroyed their grazing places,
and the remnants of peace will cease before the anger of My fury.
Like a lion He abandoned His lodging, because their land became an untrodden place before the great sword.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

“Son of man, prophesy against Israel’s shepherds. Prophesy and say to the shepherds, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: O shepherds of Israel, surely shepherds do not feed themselves? Do shepherds not feed the sheep?
Behold, you consume the milk, clothe yourselves with the wool and slaughter the fattened animal, but you do not feed My sheep.
You have not strengthened the weak, restored the sick to health, bound up the broken, brought back the wandering or sought the lost. You have worn down the strong with toil.
My sheep scattered because there were no shepherds and became food for all the field’s beasts.
My sheep scattered on every mountain and upon every high hill, and scattered over the whole face of the earth. There was no one seeking them out or turning them back.
Therefore, shepherds, hear the Lord’s word:

I live, says the Lord, the Lord: surely because My sheep became plunder and My sheep became food for all the plain’s beasts for lack of shepherds, and the shepherds did not seek out My sheep but fed themselves and did not feed My sheep—
because of this, shepherds,

thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against the shepherds. I will require My sheep from their hands and turn them aside from shepherding My sheep. The shepherds will no longer feed them. I will rescue My sheep from their mouth, and they will no longer be food for them.

And I will slaughter Judah’s counsel and Jerusalem’s counsel in this place, and cast them down by the sword before their enemies and into the hands of those seeking their lives. I will give their dead as food to the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth.
And I will make this city a ruin and a hissing. Everyone passing through it will look gloomy and hiss over its whole wound.
And they will eat the flesh of their sons and daughters, and each will eat his neighbor’s flesh in the encirclement and siege with which their enemies will besiege them.
And I will bring upon you a sword exacting the penalty of the covenant. You shall flee into your cities, and I will send death among you; you shall be handed into enemies’ hands.
When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and give back your bread by weight. You shall eat and in no wise be filled.
If after these things you do not obey Me, but walk crookedly toward Me,
then I Myself will walk with you in contrary anger, and I will discipline you seven times according to your sins.
And you shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you shall eat.
Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and said, “What are you willing to give me, and I will hand Him over to you?” They weighed out for him thirty silver coins.
From then on he sought a suitable opportunity to hand Him over.
Then Judas, who had handed Him over, saw that He had been condemned. Filled with regret, he returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders,
saying, “I sinned by handing over innocent blood.” They said, “What is that to us? See to it yourself.”
He threw the silver coins into the sanctuary and withdrew; then he went away and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the silver coins and said, “It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, because they are the price of blood.”
After taking counsel, they bought the potter’s field with them as a burial place for strangers.
Therefore that field has been called Field of Blood until today.
Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: “They took the thirty silver coins, the price of the One priced, whom some of the sons of Israel priced,
and gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord directed me.”
And if the bull gores a male slave or a female slave, he shall give thirty didrachmas of silver to their master, and the bull shall be stoned.
I am the good Shepherd; the good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.
The hired worker, who is not a shepherd and does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees—and the wolf seizes them and scatters them—
because he is a hired worker and does not care for the sheep.
Thus says the Lord God, who made heaven and fixed it in place, established the earth and its contents, and gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those treading it:
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: On that day words will rise in your heart, and you will devise evil plans,
and say, “I will go up against an abandoned land; I will come upon those resting quietly and dwelling in peace, all living in a land with no wall or bars, and they have no doors,”

to take plunder and strip their spoils, to turn your hand against the desolate land that was inhabited and against a nation gathered from many nations, acquiring possessions, dwelling upon the earth’s navel.

Saba, Daidan, Carthaginian merchants and all their villages will say to you, “Are you coming for plunder, to plunder and strip spoils? Have you gathered your assembly to take silver and gold, carry away possessions and strip spoils?”
Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog, Thus says the Lord: On that day when My people Israel are settled in peace, will you not be roused?
You will come from your place in the farthest north, with many nations beside you, all horse riders, a great assembly and a mighty force,

and come up against My people Israel like a cloud covering the land. It will be at the end of days; I will bring you against My land so that all the nations may know Me when I am sanctified in you before them.
The Lord smite you with madness, and with blindness, and with bewilderment of mind.
And you shall grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and He shall not prosper your ways; and you shall be wronged and plundered all your days, and there shall be none to help you.

The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will blaze against them and consume them, and there will be no bearer of fire in the house of Esau, because the Lord has spoken.
For by Thee I will be rescued from a raiding band, and by my God I will cross over a wall.
My God’s way is blameless; the Lord’s sayings are tried by fire; He is a protector of all who hope in Him.
For who is God except the Lord? And who is God except our God?
God girds me with power and made my way blameless,
He sets my feet firmly like a deer’s and makes me stand upon the heights,
training my hands for war; and Thou madest my arms a bronze bow.
And Thou gavest me the protection of my salvation; Thy right hand supported me, and Thy discipline set me upright completely, and Thy discipline itself will teach me.
Do not go out into a field or walk on the roads, because the enemies’ sword dwells all around.
Daughter of My people, gird yourself with sackcloth; sprinkle yourself with ashes. Make mourning for yourself for a beloved one, a pitiful lament, because misery will suddenly come upon you.
But one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
And the one who has seen has borne witness, and his testimony is true; and he knows that he speaks the truth, so that you also may believe.
For these things happened so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: “A bone of His will not be broken.”
And again another Scripture says, “They will look on the One whom they pierced.”
And the Lord’s word came to Jeremiah concerning the lack of rain:
Judea mourned, and her gates were emptied and darkened upon the earth, and Jerusalem’s cry rose.
Her magnates sent their younger ones for water; they came to wells and found no water and brought back their vessels empty.
And the land’s works failed because there was no rain; the farmers were ashamed and covered their heads.
